hypotheses.name: clogged_strainer
hypotheses.diagnostic_step: Isolate power and close any downstream valves. Remove the suction strainer (foot-valve basket or inline Y-strainer on the suction side) and inspect the mesh against a light. If a suction-side vacuum gauge is fitted, compare its reading at rated flow to baseline before removal.
hypotheses.expected_result: Mesh is at least 80 percent open with no matted algae, silt cake, or weed debris. Suction vacuum reading should be within 2 inHg (about 7 kPa) of the commissioning baseline for the same flow condition. A vacuum reading 5 inHg or more above baseline strongly indicates upstream restriction.
hypotheses.if_confirmed: Clean the strainer thoroughly with a soft brush and clean water; do not use wire brushes on stainless mesh. Replace the mesh if torn or permanently deformed. Consider fitting a coarser pre-strainer if debris load is high, and shorten the cleaning interval.
hypotheses.if_ruled_out: Suction path is clear and unrestricted. Move to impeller_damage hypothesis.

hypotheses.name: impeller_damage
hypotheses.diagnostic_step: Lock out power. Drain and open the pump casing. Inspect the impeller for cracked, chipped, or eroded vanes, particularly at the leading and trailing edges. Measure the vane-to-volute (cutwater) clearance with a feeler gauge, and check the wear ring gap.
hypotheses.expected_result: Vanes are intact and symmetric with no missing material. Cutwater clearance and wear-ring gap are within the manufacturer's tolerance, typically 0.3-0.5 mm for centrifugal irrigation pumps. No pitting from cavitation and no rope/fibre wrap around the eye.
hypotheses.if_confirmed: Replace the impeller and matching wear ring as a set. Balance-check the replacement impeller if the pump runs above 2000 rpm. Renew the mechanical seal while the pump is open, refill, prime, and verify flow against the pump curve.
hypotheses.if_ruled_out: Impeller and internals are serviceable. Move to discharge_valve_partial hypothesis.

hypotheses.name: discharge_valve_partial
hypotheses.diagnostic_step: With the pump running at normal speed, walk the discharge line and confirm every isolation valve, non-return valve, and pressure-relief valve is in the position it should be. Compare discharge pressure at the pump outlet gauge to the pump curve for the actual measured flow (bucket-and-stopwatch or flow meter).
hypotheses.expected_result: All isolation valves fully open (handle aligned with pipe run for gate/ball valves). Non-return valve clapper swings freely when tapped. Measured discharge pressure sits on the pump's published curve for the measured flow, within about 10 percent.
hypotheses.if_confirmed: Open the throttled valve fully, or repair/replace the seized non-return valve. If a pressure-relief valve is dumping, re-set it above the operating pressure per manufacturer instructions. Re-measure flow and pressure to confirm they return to the curve.
hypotheses.if_ruled_out: Discharge path is fully open and matches the pump curve. Escalate: check for a partially closed impeller-eye obstruction, worn casing, low motor RPM (measure with tachometer), or suction-side cavitation from excessive lift (defer to expert).
